thread:
alyssa: Noticing a new tail-latency bump on Mistral-7B sliding-window workloads after yesterday's kernel selector tweak.
ben: Seen logs? rough numbers?
devon: GPU p99 went from ~42ms -> ~78ms for seq=1024 steady-state. throughput steady but latency distribution widened.
alyssa: Yup. I repro'd with our streaming bench: short prefixes are fine, but when sliding-window hits wrap boundaries latency spikes.
marie: Any correlation with RoPE scaling config change last week? I thought that only affected positional remapping.
alyssa: Seems related. When rope_scale != 1.0 the kernel chooser sometimes picks the slower attention path (non-windowed fallback) for certain tile sizes.
ben: Hmm. Kernel selector heuristic prioritized kernel A for efficiency, but it had a guard that checks for pos_embed continuity. If scaled RoPE triggers a mismatch it falls back.
devon: Profile snippet from profiler (nvprof-like):
```
kernel_fast_attn: avg 1.9ms (chosen 55% of calls)
kernel_fallback_attn: avg 6.4ms (chosen 45% of calls)
KV cache memcpy: spikes at wrap-boundary + 2.1x
```
alyssa: Key point: fallback selection happens mid-sequence when sliding-window pointer wraps -> causes big memcpy and kernel recompile path.
marie: Does the runtime incorrectly compute effective max_pos or offset when rope_scale is applied? Could be off-by-one in window index math.
ben: I dug into TileChooser: it computes window_index = (global_pos + offset) / tile_len. The offset normalization assumes unscaled RoPE. If rope_scale != 1.0, the effective position space shifts and the equality check fails.
devon: Quick patch idea: normalize positions by current rope_scale when computing tile boundaries, or loosen the equality check to tolerate small shifts.
alyssa: Agreed. Also noticed batching heuristic: microbatch packing mixes sequences with different rope_scale metadata -> cache layout thrash. We should avoid packing incompatible rope_scale into same microbatch.
marie: Can we add a cheap microbatch compatibility key: (model_version, rope_scale, head_kv_dim) and forbid mixing?
ben: That'll hurt packing density but prevents fallback churn. Might need to add a packing penalty factor instead of hard forbid.
devon: Ran a small experiment: forbidding mixed rope_scale reduced p99 by ~28% for our test prompt set at cost of -12% throughput.
alyssa: For now roll out a targeted mitigation: add rope_scale to compatibility key and add a metric to track packing losses. Then we can tune packing penalty if needed.
marie: Also saw attention-mask edge-case: when users pass shorter max_position_embeddings than trained model, mask generation had inconsistent dtype leading to GPU false-branch. Fixed by casting mask to int8 before kernel.
ben: Nice catch. That bug could interact with kernel selection too (mask shape mismatch => choose safe kernel).
alyssa: Action items: 1) devon to prototype normalization patch in TileChooser and add unit test for scaled RoPE wrap boundaries. 2) ben to surface rope_scale in packing compatibility and add metric. 3) marie to push mask-dtype fix to prod. 4) infra-bot to add a canary for seq=1024 sliding-window with rope_scale !=1.0.
devon: Will open PR with tests, bench included. Expect draft in ~2h.
ben: I'll add a dashboard card showing packing reuse and p99 delta.
marie: Mask dtype fix in CI now, small patch.
infra-bot: Canary created: prow/job/infra/canaries/mistral-windowed-rope/1840124300. Alerts on p99 increase >15%.
alyssa: Thanks team. If PRs look good let's roll patch to canary primarily, then staged. Keep eyes on kernel selection traces (add tag). :thumbsup:
ben: Also logging improvement: add kernel_choice_reason field to inference trace to capture "rope_scale_mismatch" when fallback chosen. Helps postmortems.
devon: Good idea. I'll include that in the TileChooser patch.
alyssa: Otherwise looks like a combination of kernel selection heuristic + packing incompatibility + mask dtype. Patch sequence should eliminate the odd spikes.
marie: Will monitor canary and post metrics in a follow-up thread.
ben: FYI I also reproduced a minor kv-cache growth leak when fallback happens mid-stream; investigating how memcpy offsets are computed after fallback.
alyssa: Keep it small and observable. We don't want a regression during canary.
devon: PR link will include microbench results and flamegraphs.
alyssa: Great. Closing for now — ping on the PR. :wave:
